payload.name: bronchiole
payload.scope: People made the bronchiole construct to map the cartilage-free segment of the bronchial tree distal to the segmental bronchi, so that pathologists can identify the conducting-respiratory boundary and pulmonologists can categorize small-airways disease.

definition.body: The bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the cartilage-free airway branches of the bronchial tree distal to the segmental bronchi. Parameters: (1) the wall architecture — lacking hyaline cartilage plates and submucosal glands, with a wall composed of smooth muscle, elastic fibers, and a mucosal lining; (2) the epithelial lining — transitioning from pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells proximally to simple cuboidal with Club and ciliated cells distally; (3) the diameter — generally under 1 mm internal caliber, distinguishing it from the cartilage-bearing bronchi; (4) the functional classification — divided into terminal bronchioles (purely conducting) and respiratory bronchioles (transitional, with scattered gas-exchange alveoli in the wall). It persists as a maintained anatomical landmark in pulmonary histology, respiratory physiology, and clinical small-airways assessment. e.g.: the bronchiole described in Junqueira Basic Histology, 15th edition; airway resistance contribution of bronchioles per West Respiratory Physiology, 10th edition; bronchiolar smooth muscle reactivity in asthma per GINA guidelines | not: the bronchus; the alveolus [formal: bronchiolus pulmonis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.name: terminal-bronchiole
payload.scope: People made the terminal-bronchiole construct to map the last purely conducting airway of the tree, so that pathologists mark the conducting-respiratory transition and pulmonologists localize where small-airways disease begins.

definition.body: The terminal bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the most distal airway of the purely conducting portion of the bronchial tree, the airway immediately proximal to the respiratory bronchiole. Parameters: (1) the position in the conducting path — the final rung of the accepted airway hierarchy, the path running subsegmental bronchus, terminal bronchiole, respiratory bronchiole, alveolar duct, alveolar sac, alveolus, so the terminal bronchiole is the last airway before the respiratory zone begins; (2) the wall architecture — a smooth-muscle and elastic-fiber sleeve without hyaline cartilage plates and without submucosal glands, its wall perforated by no alveolar openings, which is the map's boundary: the first wall to carry scattered alveolar outpouchings is already the respiratory bronchiole; (3) the epithelial lining — simple cuboidal epithelium with ciliated and Club cells at this distal limit, the last fully ciliated airway; (4) the caliber — under 1 mm internal diameter, below the subsegmental level whose cartilage plates mark the bronchial side of the transition; (5) the functional role — the last airway contributing to conducting-zone airway resistance, so its smooth-muscle tone sets the threshold below which obstruction is a small-airways disease rather than a bronchial one. It persists as a maintained level of the named airway hierarchy in pulmonary histology, respiratory physiology, and small-airways assessment. e.g.: the terminal bronchiole section showing the bronchiolar transition in Junqueira Basic Histology 15th edition; the terminal bronchiole rung in the acinus diagram of West Respiratory Physiology 10th edition; small-airways resistance attributed to terminal bronchioles per GINA bronchial smooth-muscle assessment | not: the respiratory bronchiole (the transitional airway with scattered alveolar outpouchings on its wall); the subsegmental bronchus (the last cartilage-bearing airway proximal to this level); the alveolus (the gas-exchange sac distal to the respiratory zone) [formal: bronchiolus terminalis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.name: bronchiole
payload.scope: People made the bronchiole construct to map the cartilage-free airway segment distal to the segmental bronchi, so that histology, physiology and clinical practice can mark the conducting-respiratory boundary and categorize small-airways disease.

definition.body: The bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the human-made category of cartilage-free airway branches distal to the segmental bronchi. Parameters: (1) the maker — pulmonary histology and respiratory physiology keep the category, taught since the early 20th century and codified in histology atlases and physiology texts; (2) the boundary — it includes terminal bronchioles and respiratory bronchioles, excludes bronchi with hyaline cartilage plates and submucosal glands, and is distinguished from alveolar ducts and alveolar sacs by the presence or absence of alveolar outpouchings in the wall; (3) the persistence mechanism — the category persists through named diagrams, atlases, teaching slides and clinical small-airways assessment protocols that reference the bronchiole level as the conducting-respiratory transition. It persists as a maintained level in anatomical teaching and clinical small-airways assessment. e.g.: the bronchiole level in Junqueira Basic Histology 15th edition; the bronchiole category in West Respiratory Physiology 10th edition; bronchiolar small-airways resistance in GINA asthma guidelines | not: the bronchus (cartilage-bearing airway proximal to the bronchiole); the alveolus (gas-exchange sac distal to the respiratory bronchiole) [formal: bronchiolus pulmonis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
